General elections were held in [Palau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palau "Palau") on 5 November 2024 to elect a [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Palau "President of Palau") and the [National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palau_National_Congress "Palau National Congress").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Palauan_general_election#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Palauan_general_election#cite_note-2) Incumbent President [Surangel Whipps Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surangel_Whipps_Jr. "Surangel Whipps Jr.") faced former president [Tommy Remengesau Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Remengesau_Jr. "Tommy Remengesau Jr.") in the election, and was reelected. This was the first presidential election where Remengesau lost.
## Electoral system
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Palauan_general_election&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Electoral system")]
The president was elected using the [two-round system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-round_system "Two-round system").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Palauan_general_election#cite_note-3)
The 15 members of the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_of_Palau "Senate of Palau") were elected from a single nationwide constituency by [block voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plurality-at-large_voting "Plurality-at-large voting"), with each voter having 15 votes to cast. The 16 members of the [House of Delegates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Delegates_of_Palau "House of Delegates of Palau") were elected in single-member constituencies based on the [states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_of_Palau "States of Palau") using [first-past-the-post voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-past-the-post_voting "First-past-the-post voting").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Palauan_general_election#cite_note-4)

## Campaign
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Palauan_general_election&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Campaign")]
Campaigning was marred by diplomatic and economic issues. Tommy Remengesau Jr criticized growing security relations with the United States under Whipps' presidency, which the latter has supported as a "deterrent". Remengesau also pledged to revoke a 15% tax on goods introduced by Whipps.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Palauan_general_election#cite_note-20)
## Results
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Palauan_general_election&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Results")]
Preliminary results appeared to show Surangel Whipps Jr. leading in the presidential race,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Palauan_general_election#cite_note-21) while [Raynold Oilouch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raynold_Oilouch "Raynold Oilouch") was leading as vice president.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Palauan_general_election#cite_note-taiwan-22) Whipps formally claimed victory on 11 November, while Remengesau conceded defeat earlier.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Palauan_general_election#cite_note-23)
